item.title: A tale of two periodicities
item.description: arXiv:2611.10243v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide a common explanation for two 4-periodic phenomena arising in the study of connective real K-theory: first, the family of twists of ko over $B\mathbb Z/2$, and second, the torsion in the Picard group of $Q_1$-local $\mathcal A(1)$-modules. These phenomena have been previously studied, as they lead to 4-periodic patterns in Smith homomorphisms, resp. in the ko-homology of $(B\mathbb Z/2)^n$. In this paper, we exhibit both of these 4-periodicities as consequences of an isomorphism of two extraspecial groups of order 32.
item.dc:creator: Arun Debray, Cameron Krulewski, Natalia Pacheco-Tallaj

item.title: Persistence landscape velocity: Closed formulas and a topological probe of quantum criticality
item.description: arXiv:2611.11358v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the landscape velocity $\xi$, a scalar measure of variation of a parameter-dependent persistence landscape. For families of finite barcodes whose bars are all born at the fixed filtration value $0$, we show that $\xi$ is the $L^2$ speed of the landscape curve where the sorted death times are differentiable and derive an exact closed formula that requires no persistence landscape at all: the death times of the barcodes, as functions of the parameter, suffice. For the velocity of the empirical mean of several landscapes we also prove a closed formula which, again, strikingly requires neither the empirical mean landscape nor any of the individual landscapes, only the individual barcodes. As an application, we revisit Olsthoorn's persistent homology analysis of the transverse-field Ising chain. Whereas his approach uses different homology degrees and summaries depending on the boundary conditions, ours uses $H_0$ only and a single rule: the position of the maximum of $\xi$. This rule locates the quantum critical point for both periodic and open boundary conditions, and for both mutual-information and correlator-based dissimilarities. The position of the maximum converges to the critical point faster than all the estimators we can extract from Olsthoorn's work. In the 4 scenarios considered (different boundary conditions and different dissimilarity matrices), the peak of the normalized velocity becomes increasingly pronounced with system size, with observed logarithmic growth. This logarithmic growth is proved for periodic boundaries with correlator dissimilarity under stated hypotheses, identifying landscape velocity as a singular topological response to quantum criticality.
item.dc:creator: Francisco Belch\'i, Nahuel Statuto

item.title: Fundamental Groups of Permutation Complexes
item.description: arXiv:2611.11362v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an elementary argument showing that fundamental groups of permutation complexes are free. Hence, $\mathbb{R} P^2$ cannot be realized by a permutation complex, answering a question of Chach\'olski, Levi and Meshulam.
item.dc:creator: Dejan Govc

item.title: On Poincar\'e spaces which are not manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.11463v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This expository note gives a short derivation of the classical Spivak normal fibration formula for the total space of a spherical fibration over a Poincar\'e duality space. We review the associated smooth, PL, and topological manifold realization criteria and illustrate them with examples from the stable stems. The principal application combines these criteria with the completed solution of the Kervaire invariant problem to identify the exceptional stems in a specified family of three cell Poincar\'e spaces.
item.dc:creator: John R. Klein

item.title: Multiplicativity of the Serre Spectral Sequence in Homotopy Type Theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.11828v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Working in homotopy type theory, we define relative homotopy groups and give three equivalent definitions of the product on these groups. Using this product, we establish the multiplicativity of the cohomological Serre spectral sequence. We show a connection between the homotopy product and the cup-product in cohomology, which leads to the classically familiar description of the starting page of the spectral sequence as a tensor product of graded rings. As applications, we compute cohomology rings of several classifying spaces and loop spaces of spheres.
item.dc:creator: Arseniy Kryazhev

item.title: Discrete Configuration Spaces of Simplex Skeleta: a Middle-Dimensional Manifold Phenomenon
item.description: arXiv:2611.12847v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a simple graph $\Gamma$ without loops and an integer $n\geq2$, Abrams showed in his Ph.D. thesis that the discrete configuration space $DConf(\Gamma,n)$ is homeomorphic to a closed $n$-manifold if and only if $n=2$ and $\Gamma$ is $K_5$ or $K_{3,3}$, the two minimal obstructions to graph planarity. We show that this manifold property persists for the infinite family of discrete configuration spaces obtained by replacing the Kuratowski graphs with the $d$-skeleton of the simplex of dimension $2d+2$, thus recovering Abrams' $K_5$ case when $d=1$. Our manifold recognition argument relies on a recursive application of Whitehead's theorem that collapsible PL manifolds are PL balls, combined with Forman's discrete Morse theory. The resulting construction produces an infinite family of combinatorial spheres that contains the Legendre polytope boundaries and is closed under taking vertex links.
item.dc:creator: Emilio J. Gonz\'alez, Jes\'us Gonz\'alez, Mary Carmen P\'erez-Morales

item.title: On the homotopy automorphism group of simply-connected homology $\mathbb C \mathrm P^3$
item.description: arXiv:2611.09976v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we compute the group of homotopy equivalences of closed, smooth, simply connected $6$-manifolds whose integral homology groups are isomorphic to whose of the complex projective space $\mathbb C \mathrm P^3$, building on computations of their mapping class groups.
item.dc:creator: Matthias Kreck, Yang Su, Shengye Zhu

item.title: On the monotonicity of amenable category for geometric 4-manifolds and their connected sums
item.description: arXiv:2611.11247v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that the amenable category is monotone with respect to the domination relation for geometric $4$-manifolds and their connected sums.
item.dc:creator: Pietro Capovilla, Alberto Casali, Christoforos Neofytidis

item.title: Compact branch sets and injectivity of proper branched coverings
item.description: arXiv:2611.11844v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we show that a proper continuous open discrete map from the open unit ball $B^n$ onto a domain in $\R^n$ with $n\geq5$ is a homeomorphism whenever its branch set is compact. This answers Vuorinen's question affirmatively in every dimension $n\ge5.$ In dimension four, we also show that, under the additional assumption of quasiregularity, the map is a quasiconformal homeomorphism. Together with the three-dimensional theorem of Kauranen, Luisto and Tengvall, these results answer the quasiregular question posed as Problem~7.66 in the collections of Barth--Brannan--Hayman and Hayman--Lingham in every dimension $n\ge3$.
item.dc:creator: Deguang Zhong

item.title: $\mathrm{RO}(G)$-graded norms for de Rham-Witt forms
item.description: arXiv:2611.12043v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We make two case studies of $\mathrm{RO}(G)$-graded homotopy in connection with $p$-adic cohomology. First, we identify the $\mathrm{RO}(\mathbf T)$-graded $\mathrm{TC}^-$ and $\mathrm{TP}$ of quasiregular semiperfectoid rings as multi-Rees algebras for the Nygaard and $\phi^\bullet(I)$-adic filtrations. We additionally compute $E^{h\mathbf T}_\bigstar$ and $E^{t\mathbf T}_\bigstar$ when $E$ is a general even $\mathbf E_\infty$-ring with $\mathbf T$-action, and compute $(\mathrm{TR}^n)^{h\mathbf T/C_{p^n}}_\bigstar$ in terms of iterated Nygaard filtrations. Next, we compute the $\mathrm{RO}(\mathbf Z_p)^\land$-graded $\mathrm{TR}$ of smooth algebras over a perfectoid base, providing a pushout of the works of Hesselholt and Angeltveit-Gerhardt along the base case $\mathbf F_p$. Using this, we extend Angeltveit's Norm map of Witt vectors to the de Rham-Witt complex, which participates in a "Witt coordinates" decomposition of the $p$-primary Adams operations.
item.dc:creator: Yuri J. F. Sulyma

item.title: Global Green-Schwarz response on quaternionic sphere bundles
item.description: arXiv:2611.12810v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Local anomaly polynomials describe local variations, but a normalized Green-Schwarz phase also depends on global background data. We explain this dependence for ten-dimensional three-sphere bundles of quaternionic lines over closed spin seven-manifolds. The backgrounds retain two specified $\mathrm{Spin}(16)$ gauge bundles and an integral differential trivialization on the base, including its boundary identifications. The trivialized class is the sum of half the first Pontryagin class of the tangent bundle and the second Chern class of the quaternionic line's underlying complex bundle. For these backgrounds, the calculation combines a generally nonzero local Green-Schwarz integral with a real eta invariant evaluated by a twelve-dimensional Atiyah-Patodi-Singer filling. Together, these terms determine an integral relative characteristic number; the additive response is one third of that number, modulo integers. When the base's third and fourth rational cohomology groups vanish, the response equals eight times the Crowley-Goette invariant, without assuming that the base is simply connected. A calibration using the actual quaternionic line bundle gives additive value one third on $\mathrm{Sp}(2)$, recovering the known third-root phase. Distinct integral String data on one fixed ten-manifold give all three phase values, showing which global background information the response can detect. The physical identifications retain their prescribed fermion data, while the separate application to integral topological modular forms and vertex operator superalgebras requires compatible integral lifts. The response calculation constructs neither a microscopic realization nor an equivalence of complete theories.
item.dc:creator: Yuqi Li, Hao-Yu Sun

item.title: Coarse Embeddings Beyond Doubling: Persistence Diagrams and Multiparameter Modules
item.description: arXiv:2611.12866v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study coarse embeddings into Hilbert space and the asymptotic dimension of spaces of persistence diagrams and multiparameter persistence modules. We replace doubling, the usual hypothesis for landmark embeddings, by admissible tent covers of bounded multiplicity at every scale: stacking them across dyadic scales gives an explicit $1$-Lipschitz coarse embedding, with lower gauge $c\sqrt{\tau t}$, or nearly linear for slowly decaying weights, and the same covers bound the asymptotic dimension by the multiplicity. The spaces of persistence diagrams are not doubling but carry such covers, and for diagrams with $n$ points our covers improve the constant of the known landmark embedding by a factor exponential in $n$. Slice by slice, the construction embeds multiparameter modules with boundedly many bars per slice under the matching distance on any finite net of slices, a class that contains the modules with at most $n$ generators. Bounding bars or persistent Betti numbers instead of generators fails: two-parameter modules with one bar on every slice have infinite asymptotic dimension, and neither they nor the modules of bounded support and bounded rank admit a coarse embedding into Hilbert space, under the matching or the interleaving distance.
item.dc:creator: Sushovan Majhi, Atish Mitra, \v{Z}iga Virk

item.title: Foliated and compactly supported isotopies of tubular neighborhoods
item.description: arXiv:2208.05876v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a foliation with a "singular" submanifold $\Sigma$ on a smooth manifold $A$ and $p:E \to \Sigma$ be a tubular neighborhood of $\Sigma$ in $A$. Under certain "scalability" assumptions on $\mathcal{F}$ near $\Sigma$, we prove that every leaf preserving diffeomorphism $h$ of $A$ is isotopic via a leaf preserving isotopy to a diffeomorphism which coincides with some vector bundle morphism of $E$ near $\Sigma$. This result is simultaneously a foliated, compactly supported and parametrized variant of a well known statement that every diffeomorphism $h$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$ fixing the origin is isotopic to the linear isomorphism induced by its Jacobi matrix at $0$. Particular cases of such a "linearization theorem" allowed recently to compute homotopy types of leaf preserving diffeomorphism groups of polar Morse-Bott foliations on lens spaces and the twisted bundle $S^2\tilde{\times}S^1$. In general, that "linearization theorem" can be used to reduce the study of the homotopy type of the group of leaf preserving diffeomorphisms of $\mathcal{F}$ to an investigation of the following three groups (being independent in a certain sense): (a) diffeomorphism group of $\Sigma$, (b) the group of leaf preserving vector bundle isomorphisms of $E$, and (c) the group of leaf preserving diffeomorphisms of $A$ supported in $A\setminus \Sigma$, i.e. out of the "singularity" $\Sigma$.
item.dc:creator: Oleksandra Khokhliuk, Sergiy Maksymenko

item.title: On the Drinfeld formal group
item.description: arXiv:2403.02555v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We identify Drinfeld's formal group on the prismatization of $\mathrm{Spf}\,\mathbb{Z}_p$ with a formal group arising from homotopy theory, given locally by the Quillen formal group of a decompleted variant of topological periodic cyclic homology. We also prove that this formal group extends to the syntomization of $\mathrm{Spf}\,\mathbb{Z}_p$, and that it admits a certain algebraization conjectured by Drinfeld.
item.dc:creator: Deven Manam

item.title: Secondary Stiefel-Whitney numbers and corresponding cobordism groups
item.description: arXiv:2512.06371v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For every relation $R$ between Stiefel-Whitney numbers of closed $(n+1)$-manifolds we consider an associated invariant $\varkappa_R$ of null-cobordant $n$-manifolds with a certain additional structure. For $n=2k-1$ and $R = w_{n+1}+v_k^2$ the invariant $\varkappa_R$ equals the Kervaire semi-characteristic. In addition, we construct the cobordism group $\Omega_n^R$, which extends the unoriented cobordism group $\Omega_n^O$. We show that $\varkappa_R$ is a complete invariant of $R$-cobordism classes of null-cobordant $n$-manifolds. We prove that our invariant $\varkappa_R$ and $R$-cobordism class of manifold are quadratic in the sense of Gusarov-Vassiliev-Podkorytov.
item.dc:creator: Viktor Lavrukhin

item.title: Conservative geometric functors via purity
item.description: arXiv:2602.14886v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish a criterion for determining when a family of geometric functors is jointly conservative through the lens of purity in compactly generated triangulated categories. We introduce the notion of pure descendability and we apply it to two particular situations involving sequential limits of ring spectra.
item.dc:creator: Nat\`alia Castellana, Juan Omar G\'omez

item.title: Cores and localizations of $(\infty,\infty)$-categories
item.description: arXiv:2603.11005v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider $(\infty,d)$-categories in the limit $d\to \infty$ via the core or localization functors that forget or invert higher non-invertible arrows, respectively. We compare the two resulting $(\infty,1)$-categories of $(\infty,\infty)$-categories and exhibit the localization-limit as a reflective localization of the core-limit. Furthermore, we study notions of invertibility that only emerge at $d=\infty$ and give rise to intermediate reflective localizations between the two limits. For example, we characterize coinductive completion and the maps it inverts, and reveal a new separation beyond the one of Henry--Loubaton by showing that even the stronger $\omega$-completeness does not suffice to carve out the localization-limit.
item.dc:creator: Viktoriya Ozornova, Martina Rovelli, Tashi Walde

item.title: Topological symmetric and braid homologies
item.description: arXiv:2605.22946v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We identify topological symmetric homology as the free $\mathbb{E}_\infty$-algebra on an $\mathbb{E}_1$-algebra and topological braid homology as the free $\mathbb{E}_2$-algebra on an $\mathbb{E}_1$-algebra. In this way, topological symmetric homology and topological braid homology can be regarded as variants of $1$-dimensional representation homology. In order to identify topological braid homology as the free $\mathbb{E}_2$-algebra on an $\mathbb{E}_1$-algebra, we prove that the $\mathbb{E}_2$-monoidal envelope of the associative operad can be identified with the braided crossed simplicial group. Using this, we also compute the topological braid homology of grouplike $\mathbb{E}_1$-spaces. Further, we develop computational tools for topological symmetric and braid homologies. These tools allow us to perform low-degree computations of topological symmetric homology and prove that it is not Morita invariant. We also compute the topological $\Delta \mathbf{G}$-homology of Thom spectra in general and produce explicit formulas in the case of topological symmetric and braid homologies.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Angelini-Knoll, David Chan, Teena Gerhardt, Mona Merling, Maximilien P\'eroux

item.title: Rational homotopy theory of flag manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2609.30591v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $G/P$ be a flag manifold with $G$ simple. We determine the rational homotopy groups $\pi _{\ast }(G/P)\otimes \mathbb{Q}$ and describe the rational cohomology ring $H^{\ast }(G/P;\mathbb{Q})$ solely in terms of the rational homotopy types of $G$ and $P$, respectively. The proof is based on the restrictions of basic Weyl invariants of $G$ to suitable simple factors of $P$, which also address a key nonvanishing issue not settled by earlier approaches of Meier, Shiga-Tezuka, Kotschick, and Terzic.
item.dc:creator: Haibao Duan

item.title: On the hit problem of rank five
item.description: arXiv:2609.32475v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $P_q$ be the graded polynomial algebra $\mathbb F_2[x_1,x_2,\ldots ,x_q]$ over the prime field of two elements, $\mathbb F_2$, with the degree of each $x_i$ being 1. We study the {\it hit Peterson problem} of finding a minimal set of generators for $P_q$ as a module over the mod-$2$ Steenrod algebra, $\mathcal{A}.$ In this note, we present the minimal sets of $\mathcal{A}$-generators for $P_5$ in the cases where the degree are sufficiently general.
item.dc:creator: Nguyen Sum

item.title: Cohomological non-rigidity of toric manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2609.39707v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For every integer $d\geq4$, we construct pairs of projective toric manifolds of complex dimension $d$ that are not homotopy equivalent but have isomorphic integral cohomology rings and homotopy equivalent 5-fold suspensions. We also construct pairs of quasitoric manifolds over the $d$-dimensional cube with these properties. Our construction starts with a closed, oriented smooth manifold $B$ of real dimension $6$ whose integral cohomology ring is generated by $H^2(B)$. For a class $u\in H^2(B)$, let $L_u$ denote the complex line bundle with first Chern class $u$, and set $P_u=\mathbb P_B(L_0\oplus L_u)$. We show that if $u,v\in H^2(B)$ satisfy $uv=0$, then, for every finite product $N$ of complex projective spaces, the manifolds $P_{u+v}\times N$ and $P_{u-v}\times N$ have isomorphic integral cohomology rings and homotopy equivalent 5-fold suspensions. To distinguish their homotopy types, we introduce the sets of strong zero-product pairs $\mathrm{SZ}^{n,m}(X)\subseteq H^n(X)\times H^m(X)$, which are preserved by homotopy equivalences. Using these sets, we give explicit conditions on $u$ and $v$ ensuring that these manifolds are not homotopy equivalent, and exhibit toric and quasitoric examples satisfying these conditions.
item.dc:creator: Xin Fu, Tao Gong, Sergei O. Ivanov, Yingxin Li

item.title: Poincar\'e duality and module topological complexity
item.description: arXiv:2610.04153v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For every simply connected space $X$ of finite rational type with Poincar\'e duality cohomology, we prove $MTC(X)=TC_0(X)=TC_0^M(X)$: module, rational and monoidal rational topological complexity coincide. Neither formality nor finiteness of the total rational homotopy is required. For every rationally retractive map $f$ between simply connected spaces of finite rational type, we prove $relcat(f_Q)\le msecat(f_Q)+1$. This bound is sharp for rationally retractive maps. Both proofs reduce to the same question: can a module nullhomotopy taking values in a split Sullivan model be chosen with values in its kernel ideal? Comparing resolutions of consecutive ideal powers achieves this after increasing the exponent by one; for diagonals, Poincar\'e duality preserves the exponent. An ideal-preserving form of Hess's construction then converts the module nullhomotopy into a compatible algebra retraction.
item.dc:creator: Paul-Eug\`ene Parent

item.title: Complete $RO$-Graded Tambara Functor of $H\underline{\mathbb Z}$ for cyclic groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.37885v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We compute the $RO$-graded Tambara functor of $H\underline{\mathbb{Z}}$ for every finite cyclic group. We introduce a valuation language for homotopy groups to give the explicit formula for products, restrictions, transfers, Weyl actions, and norms. Besides the computation, We also develop a theory that reconstructs a genuine equivariant spectrum as the homotopy limit of a finite diagram of homotopy fixed-point spectra, Tate spectra, and only one localization spectrum at the terminal of the diagram. We call it the Tate compression theory. From it we also give a filtration for $\pi_\star(H\underline{\mathbb{Z}})$, compatible with products, restrictions, transfers, Weyl actions, and norms.
item.dc:creator: Dongming Zhang

item.title: On some formality criteria for DG-Lie algebras
item.description: arXiv:1310.3048v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give some formality criteria for a differential graded Lie algebra to be formal. For instance, we show that a DG-Lie algebra L is formal if and only if the natural spectral sequence computing the Chevalley-Eilenberg cohomology H(L,L) degenerates at second page.
item.dc:creator: Marco Manetti

item.title: On Noetherianity of tensor modules and homology of subalgebras of vector fields
item.description: arXiv:2211.08510v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that finite tensor products $\otimes_{i=1}^{r}\mathcal{T}_{\lambda}$ of modules of tensor fields are Noetherian modules over any Lie subalgebra of finite codimension in the Lie algebra of polynomial vector fields on $\mathbb{R}^n$. Moreover, the Hilbert series of their graded submodules are rational functions whose denominators are products of factors of the form $(1-t^m)$. As a corollary, we prove the conjecture of I.\,M. Gelfand, announced at the ICM in Nice in 1970, on the finite-dimensionality of the continuous cohomology of graded Lie subalgebras of finite codimension in the Lie algebra of formal vector fields $\mathcal{W}_n$. We also prove that tensor products of modules of densities are Noetherian over the Witt Lie algebra of polynomial vector fields on the punctured line. Moreover, for a weight $\lambda\neq0,1$ every nonzero submodule of the symmetric power $S^r(\mathcal{T}_\lambda)$ contains $\Delta^{2d}S^r(\mathcal{T}_\lambda)$, where $\Delta$ is the Vandermonde determinant. As a consequence, we show that a conjecture of Etingof implies the conjecture of Petukhov and Sierra on the simplicity of the quotients $U(\vir)/(C-c)$ of the enveloping algebra of the Virasoro algebra.
item.dc:creator: Boris Feigin, Alexei Kanel-Belov, Anton Khoroshkin

item.title: From Hopf Algebras in Model Categories to Hopf Algebras in $\infty$-categories
item.description: arXiv:2509.13602v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that algebra objects in model categories can be transferred to algebra objects in $\infty$-categories, without any cofibrancy or fibrancy assumptions on the algebra. We furthermore show under some mild extra assumptions that this correspondence extends to commutative bialgebras and to commutative Hopf algebras.
item.dc:creator: Inbar Klang, Josefien Kuijper, Cary Malkiewich, David Mehrle, Thor Wittich

item.title: Embedding Calculus, Goodwillie Calculus and Link Invariants
item.description: arXiv:2511.04582v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study Goodwillie-Weiss embedding calculus through its relationship with Goodwillie's functor calculus. Specifically, building on a result of Tillmann and Weiss, we construct a functorial complement for \(T_{n}\)-embeddings that takes values in Heuts's categorical \(n\)-excisive approximation of pointed spaces. We also establish an analogue of Stallings' theorem for lower central series in the context of \(T_{n}\)-embeddings of \(P \times I\) into \(D^{d}\) for any compact manifold \(P\). As an application, we show that the embedding tower of string links detects Milnor invariants.
item.dc:creator: Hyeonhee Jin

item.title: Effective Resistance in Simplicial Complexes: Generalizations and Properties
item.description: arXiv:2511.10749v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Originally introduced in circuit theory, the notion of effective resistance has been fruitfully exploited in graph theory, where each edge in a graph is understood as a resistor in an electric network. In this context, the effective resistance between two vertices quantifies the total opposition to current flow when a unit current is injected at one vertex and extracted at the other. As such, it encodes rich structural and geometric information about the underlying graph: it satisfies a minimum-energy principle termed Thomson's principle, defines a metric on the vertex set, relates to the topology of the graph through Foster's theorem, and determines the probability of appearance of an edge in a random spanning tree. Generalizations of effective resistance to simplicial complexes have been proposed in several forms, often formulated as matrix products of standard operators associated with the complex. We introduce a novel, basis-independent bilinear form, derived from an algebraic reinterpretation of circuit theory, that extends the classical effective resistance from graphs to simplicial complexes. This bilinear form acts on chains and cochains, and in particular, simplices and cosimplices in a simplicial complex. Our framework subsumes and unifies all existing matrix-based formulations of effective resistance. Moreover, we establish higher-order analogues of several fundamental properties known in the graph case: (i) we extend Thomson's principle to our basis-free framework; (ii) we establish metric properties for the effective resistance and its square root on chains and cycles, recovering the classical graph case; (iii) we provide a generalization of Foster's theorem to simplicial complexes; and (iv) we prove a matrix-tree theorem for higher-dimensional spanning trees, linking effective resistance to the probability of appearance of a simplex in random simplicial spanning trees.
item.dc:creator: In\'es Garc\'ia-Redondo, Claudia Landi, Sarah Percival, Anda Skeja, Bei Wang, Ling Zhou

item.title: Path Types in Algebraic Type Theory
item.description: arXiv:2601.06567v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A new approach to the semantics of identity types in intensional Martin-L\"of type theory is proposed, assuming only a category with finite limits and an interval. The specification of \emph{extensional} identity types in the original presentation of natural models paralleled that of the other type formers $\Sigma$ and $\Pi$, but the treatment of the \emph{intensional} case there was less uniform. It was later reformulated to an account based on polynomials; here a further improvement in the style of the other type formers is achieved by employing an interval, in order to give a single pullback specification of a model with \emph{path types}. The interval is also used to specify a (Hurewicz) fibration structure on the universe of the model. It is shown that the combination of these two conditions suffices to model the intensional identity rules, assuming only finite limits. The addition of an interval also relates the current treatment to that of cubical type theory.
item.dc:creator: Steve Awodey, Joseph Hua

item.title: Some examples of DG-Lie formality transfer
item.description: arXiv:2601.19698v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give a convenient reformulation, a slight generalization and some applications of the formality transfer theorem for DG-Lie algebras.
item.dc:creator: Marco Manetti, Gabriele Rossetti

item.title: Magnitude homology of real hyperplane arrangements
item.description: arXiv:2604.03718v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We define and study the magnitude and magnitude homology of real hyperplane arrangements by regarding their tope graphs as metric spaces. Since magnitude is a refinement of the cardinality, this may be viewed as a natural generalization of the classical problem of counting the chambers of an arrangement. Our central result is a structure theorem asserting that the magnitude and magnitude homology of an arrangement decompose into contributions indexed by its faces. In particular, the magnitude is determined by the intersection lattice of the arrangement. We also observe several interesting phenomena, including a characterization of Boolean arrangements in terms of diagonality and a reciprocity theorem reminiscent of Ehrhart--Macdonald reciprocity. Finally, based on explicit computations, we conjecture that the magnitude homology of an arrangement is torsion-free and determined by its intersection lattice.
item.dc:creator: Junnosuke Koizumi, Ye Liu

item.title: No Triangulation Without Representation: Generalization in Topological Deep Learning
item.description: arXiv:2605.06467v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Despite an ever-increasing interest in topological deep learning models that target higher-order datasets, there is no consensus on how to evaluate such models. This is exacerbated by the fact that topological objects permit operations, such as structural refinements, that are not appropriate for graph data. In this work, we extend MANTRA, a benchmark dataset containing manifold triangulations, to a larger class of manifolds with more diverse homeomorphism types. We show that, contrary to prior claims, graph neural networks can saturate the benchmark, while higher-order message passing methods lag behind. However, we find that this is contingent on the right representation and feature assignment, emphasizing their importance in baseline models. Hence, we present a novel evaluation protocol based on representational diversity and triangulation refinement. Even when including refinement-like changes in the training data, existing models fail to generalize beyond the combinatorial structure of the data. This points towards a research gap in developing models that understand topological structure independent of scale. Our work thus provides the necessary scaffolding to evaluate future models and enable the development of topology-aware inductive biases.
item.dc:creator: Johannes S. Schmidt, Martin Carrasco, Ernst R\"oell, Guy Wolf, Nello Blaser, Bastian Rieck

item.title: Triangulation of orbifolds with corners
item.description: arXiv:2610.31001v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that every compact orbifold with corners admits a triangulation compatible with all its corners: for every $k\ge1$, each connected component of the $k$-corners maps onto the image of a subcomplex, and every open simplex lies in the set of points of a single depth. Faces need not be embedded, and the local groups may permute boundary components. The proof turns the boundary hyperplanes of linear charts into mirrors by means of the squaring map, which, unlike the folding $y\mapsto|y|$, is compatible with smooth changes of charts, and then applies the triangulation theorem for orbit spaces of proper Lie groupoids.
item.dc:creator: Hao Yu

item.title: A proof of the sharpness conjectures for all saturated fusion systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.02043v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove the D\'iaz$\unicode[Arial]{x2013}$Park conjecture for sharpness of saturated fusion systems. More generally, for every saturated fusion system $\mathcal F$ over a finite $p$-group and every Mackey functor for $\mathcal F$ over the localisation $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$ of the integers at $p$, the higher limits of its contravariant part over the centric orbit category vanish in all positive degrees. In particular, the subgroup and normaliser decompositions of every $p$-local finite group $(S,\mathcal F,\mathcal L)$ over the $\mathcal F$-centric subgroups are sharp. This answers in the affirmative a question in the list of important open problems in [M. Aschbacher, R. Kessar and B. Oliver, Fusion Systems in Algebra and Topology, Cambridge Univ. Press (2011)], and proves the sharpness conjecture stated in [M. Aschbacher and B. Oliver, Fusion systems, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. (2016)] and Conjecture 1.2 of [E. Yal\c{c}$\unicode[Arial]{x131}$n, Higher limits over the fusion orbit category, Adv. Math. (2022)]. The proof is algebraic and does not rely on the classification of finite simple groups.
